req: All flaggers must complete the ATSSA Flagger Training course before beginning work; completion records kept on file (quoted from an ALDOT debris-removal contract document, not the general standard specifications)
source: ALDOT Contractual Documents ... Debris Removal (as reproduced by the Work Zone Safety Information Clearinghouse)

req: Flaggers must hold a current certification from the DOT&PF list
accepted: IMSA Flagging Level I; ATSSA Flagger Certification; ATSSA Traffic Control Supervisor; IMSA Work Zone Safety Specialist; ATSSA Flagging Instructor
source: Alaska DOT&PF Standard Specifications for Highway Construction, Flagging provision

req: All flaggers must be trained prior to starting work in the field (ARDOT employee Safety Manual; contractor rule not confirmed)
Uniformed flaggers must have successfully completed flagger training by ATSSA, the National Safety Council, or other training approved by the Engineer; certificate to the Engineer before work
source: CTDOT Standard Specifications Form 819 (2024), Uniformed Flagger

req: Flaggers on state-maintained roadways must be certified by a DelDOT-recognized program and carry the flagger certification card and photo ID
accepted: ATSSA (classroom or online), OnlineFlagger.com, LIUNA Work Zone Safety Program
source: Delaware MUTCD Section 6E.01 Standard (DE revision); DelDOT memo Acceptable Flagger Certification (11/01/2016)

req: Flaggers on the State Highway System need training and a certificate, for contract or permit work (utilities included); work can be suspended without a certified flagger
accepted: ATSSA or National Safety Council programs

req: All flaggers shall be certified by an agency approved by the Department
accepted: ATSSA, National Safety Council, Illinois Laborers' & Contractors' Joint Apprenticeship Program (contract and permit work)

req: Flagging supervised by a certified worksite traffic supervisor or a flagger certified by ATSSA or approved equal; supervisor ensures flaggers are trained
Flaggers trained before flagging (Iowa DOT flagger materials, MUTCD Part 6); employer issues a flagger training card; not required for short time, emergency or relief assignment
validity: card expires December 31 of the year after the training date
accepted: Iowa DOT flagger training card issued by the employer

req: Flaggers trained in MUTCD Part 6 flagger procedures and the KDOT Flagger Handbook; carry a card with name and training date
All flaggers trained in current MUTCD flagging procedures; proof available
validity: credentials current within the last 5 years

req: All flaggers shall be qualified (ATSSA-type course or a course approved by the LADOTD Work Zone Task Force)
source: LADOTD Temporary Traffic Control General Notes sheet (02-07-2025)

req: Flagger certification required on MaineDOT state/federal-funded projects; state law since 1991 requires privately employed flaggers to have MUTCD-consistent training
Flaggers must complete the SHA or ATSSA flagger course before working in Maryland work zones (flagger card); emergency: non-approved flagger up to 15 minutes
source: Maryland SHA Frequently Asked Work Zone Questions

req: MassDOT flagger certification: first aid/CPR, work zone safety and flagger training, 50-question exam passed at 80%
accepted: NSC, ATSSA, OSHA Training Institute or equivalent approved program

req: Traffic regulators must complete traffic regulator training (state video + MDOT Traffic Regulator's Instruction Manual)
validity: training no more than 12 months before regulating traffic
source: MDOT Work Zone Safety and Mobility Manual Section 1.05.03

req: Flaggers and pilot drivers must attend training by a MnDOT-qualified flagger trainer; Flagger Qualification Card or checklist to the Engineer
source: MnDOT Special Provisions Section I.1 (trunk highway projects)

req: Flaggers must have proof of certification and ID while flagging
accepted: ATSSA; MDOT-recognized industry association training; MDOT training

req: Valid flagger certification card (training by a qualified person in flagging and MUTCD Chapter 6), given to the engineer before flagging
Flaggers currently certified through the Montana flagger program, ATSSA, or the Idaho, Oregon or Washington programs; carry proof
Only certified flaggers may flag except emergencies or situations under 15 minutes; view The Flagger video and pass exam at 80%; contractor trains/certifies; carry card and Flagger's Handbook
accepted: unexpired cards issued by other contractors accepted

req: Flaggers shall have completed an approved instructional course in flagger procedures; valid flagger card from NDOT course or NDOT-approved course
source: NDOT Standard Specifications for Road and Bridge Construction

req: Contractor submits flagger training card before flagger work
Flaggers adequately trained by recognized programs (ATSSA, NSC, unions, construction industry associations) or by a certified flagger instructor; roster of credentialed flaggers to the Engineer
All personnel flagging, spotting or operating AFADs must complete an NCDOT-approved flagger course
source: NCDOT Work Zone Safety Qualification and Training Program

req: Pass a written examination (ndsc.org) before flagging; written verification to the Engineer
Ohio does not require flagger certification or registration (flaggers should be trained)
source: Ohio LTAP, Flagging Operations on 2-lane Rural Roads

req: A flagger should be trained in safe traffic control practices and public contact techniques (guideline; no card rule found)
source: ODOT Guidelines for Temporary Traffic Control

req: Flaggers must have completed an approved flagging course within the past 3 years and hold a current card; Oregon, Washington, Idaho or Montana certification accepted; age 18+
source: ODOT Standard Specifications 00223.30; Oregon Temporary Traffic Control Handbook 2026 sections 3.2-3.3

req: Flaggers must have completed a flagger training course meeting PennDOT minimum guidelines within the last 3 years; wallet card or roster
Certificate from a RIDOT-approved course; know the FHWA flagging handbook
accepted: National Safety Council, ATSSA, N.E. Laborers Union Training Academy

req: Flaggers must complete a flagger training course from an SCDOT-approved provider
accepted: ATSSA, Carolinas AGC, ITRE (NC State), J.M. Teague, Southeastern Chapter NSC, Tri-County Technical College
source: SCDOT Flagger's Handbook; SCDOT Approved Work Zone Traffic Control Training Guidelines

req: Flaggers must be certified in South Dakota before flagging on a Department project (course + written test); age 18+; carry proof
source: SDDOT Standard Specifications for Roads & Bridges, C. Flagging

req: Flaggers trained and certified in flagging operations by an approved program
accepted: ATSSA, National Safety Council, TTAP, ABET-accredited university programs, or Department-approved program

req: Contractor designates in writing a flagger instructor who serves as flagging supervisor and trains flaggers; list of certified flaggers before work begins; TxDOT keeps a list of approved flagger courses
source: TxDOT Standard Specifications, Flaggers (Item 7 section 2.6.2 as quoted)

req: Flaggers must be trained and certified before flagging in a work zone; official course by a certified instructor
accepted: programs listed in UDOT Standard Specification 01554
source: UDOT Flagger Training & Certification page; UDOT Flagger Handbook

req: 4-hour course by a certified instructor (AGC of Vermont, ATSSA or NSC instructor courses); carry proof
Certified through the VDOT Flagger Certification Program, ATSSA, or another VDOT-approved program; carry a readable card
validity: VDOT flagger card 2 years; VDOT Basic/Intermediate work zone course or ATSSA classroom 4 years
source: Virginia Work Area Protection Manual Section 6E.01

req: All flaggers shall possess a current flagging card issued by Washington, Oregon, Montana or Idaho (WSDOT spec); state safety rule WAC 296-155-305(6): valid Washington card or reciprocity-state card
validity: card expires no more than 3 years after issue

req: Flaggers must be certified by passing ATSSA training
Since January 1, 2020 all flaggers on Wisconsin state highways must be certified (training meeting the Wisconsin Flagging Handbook)
Complete and pass a training program approved by the State Construction Office before flagging (3-day grace in unplanned emergencies); current card on the project
accepted: Wyoming Flaggers Traffic Control Certification, ATSSA

req: Flaggers shall be certified by ATSSA or another agency approved by the Engineer
source: DDOT Standard Specifications for Highways and Structures (2013), Flagger Certification

req: Nationally recognized Work Zone Traffic Control Safety - Flagger training and certification meeting MUTCD (quoted from one HDOT Highways Division contract addendum, Island of Hawaii)
validity: certification completed within a maximum of 4 years
source: HDOT Highways Division contract addendum (as reproduced by the Clearinghouse)

req: Flagger certification from an ITD-approved course by an ITD-approved instructor (Evergreen Safety Council and ATSSA courses approved); ITD accepts Washington, Oregon and Montana cards under a multi-state agreement, and Utah under a separate agreement
source: Idaho Transportation Department, Flagger and Traffic Control Supervisor Certification and Reciprocity Information

req: To get or renew CDOT flagger certification: at least 18, trained by a CDOT-authorized entity, pass a closed-book exam; flaggers must speak and understand English (Jan 2026 memo); fluorescent red apparel not allowed for flaggers in Colorado
source: CDOT Flagger Program FAQs; CDOT Flagger Program industry memo January 2026
